synthesis.trait: Uses a firearm and aggressive physical posture to confront a perceived threat to Cheyenne
Displays swaggering, foul-mouthed cynicism about cops/authority
Shows genuine tenderness and concern for Cheyenne beneath his tough exterior

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Uses a firearm and aggressive physical posture to confront a perceived threat to Cheyenne
turning_points.what_changes: O'Shea moves from merely drawing his gun and exiting the car (a threat posture) to actively pressing the gun to John's head and physically shoving him against a wall -- direct escalation from readiness to active aggression. But John instantly disarms him and has him on his knees about to break his arm, exposing that his aggressive posture is bravado without real capability against a trained opponent.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Uses a firearm and aggressive physical posture to confront a perceived threat to Cheyenne
turning_points.what_changes: Direct, unbroken continuation of the disarming: John empties O'Shea's gun and pockets the bullets, then tosses the weapon out the window, and O'Shea sits 'a bit emasculated' -- deepening the same exposed limit from the immediately preceding beat rather than a new event.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Shows genuine tenderness and concern for Cheyenne beneath his tough exterior
turning_points.what_changes: In the same unbroken exchange immediately following his admission that he's trying to help Cheyenne forget her hell, O'Shea continues by conceding 'I ain't proud to say it' -- extending the same moment of genuine vulnerability rather than starting a new one.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Shows genuine tenderness and concern for Cheyenne beneath his tough exterior
turning_points.what_changes: Immediately after voicing his own shame, O'Shea visibly softens and sighs in direct response to Cheyenne's pleading look -- the same emotional thread continuing to its point of surrender just before he discloses what he knows.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Uses a firearm and aggressive physical posture to confront a perceived threat to Cheyenne
turning_points.what_changes: O'Shea's protection of Cheyenne shifts from physical bravado (gun to John's head) to a qualitatively different and higher-cost act: self-incriminating disclosure of the Reggie/Mackie shakedown, exposing himself to real retaliation risk he never faced when merely brandishing a weapon.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Uses a firearm and aggressive physical posture to confront a perceived threat to Cheyenne
turning_points.what_changes: The same disclosure continues without a gap, O'Shea specifying the exact pharmaceutical/military-grade goods demanded and the threat Reggie and Mackie made to pin Holly's disappearance on him -- deepening the same risky confession.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Uses a firearm and aggressive physical posture to confront a perceived threat to Cheyenne
turning_points.what_changes: The confession sequence concludes with O'Shea explicitly naming the mortal stakes of what he's just done ('Sucka got shot in the face, yo!') -- the same unbroken disclosure reaching its clearest statement of personal risk.

turning_points.trait_it_relates_to: Uses a firearm and aggressive physical posture to confront a perceived threat to Cheyenne
turning_points.what_changes: The identical gun that John confiscated and emptied earlier is now handed back to O'Shea, and instead of using it aggressively he simply pockets it and gently walks Cheyenne home ('C'mon, babe. Let's go.') -- a concrete, prop-based reversal of the earlier disarming, completing his arc from weapon-wielding aggressor to trusted, gentle presence.
